strategy: Run the cartservice memory-exhaustion test first, then wait for recovery and a healthy baseline before testing paymentservice failure; do not overlap faults. The two distinct experiment types cover resource exhaustion and errors, but the exact two-experiment budget does not allow a third failure class.

spec.reason: cartservice is a single replica with 1.0 reach across all five flows, is shared by frontend and checkoutservice, and has a 128 Mi memory limit. A prior 110 MB run caused errors across all flows, guard abort, and a 41-second recovery, so this is a high-risk, shopper-visible test of OOM behavior.
spec.hypothesis: Allocating 110 MB inside cartservice will exhaust its available memory, trigger errors across the shop, and likely cause the safety guard to abort the fault; the service may need time to recover.

experiments.learning_goal: Measure the cartservice OOM blast radius and recovery time after memory pressure.

spec.reason: paymentservice is a single replica on the checkout path. Past 30-second failures visibly affected checkout and reached 21–25% peak error rates, sometimes triggering the guard; this tests the shopper impact of losing payment processing, on a different service and with a different fault type from the first experiment.
spec.hypothesis: While paymentservice is unavailable, checkout attempts will fail, but other flows should remain largely unaffected; the error-rate guard is likely to abort the experiment.

experiments.learning_goal: Measure checkout’s error response and the guard’s behavior when the payment dependency is unavailable.

skipped_ideas.idea: Add a third experiment from a third failure class, such as a controlled slowdown test.
skipped_ideas.why_not: The plan is limited to exactly two experiments, so a third distinct failure class cannot fit the budget.

skipped_ideas.idea: Add 300 ms network delay to productcatalogservice.
skipped_ideas.why_not: Past evidence shows even 100 ms adds roughly 700 ms to pages through sequential calls; the stronger delay risks a guard-triggering slowdown that teaches little.
A prior run already tripped the p95 guard after a few seconds, so it is likely to produce a brief, guard-limited slowdown rather than a useful additional result.
